title: Efficacy of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Depression: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Background: Depression is a major public health concern. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) has shown promise as a treatment option. Methods: We conducted a double-blind randomized controlled trial with 300 participants diagnosed with major depressive disorder. Participants were randomly assigned to CBT (n=150) or waitlist control (n=150). The primary outcome was change in Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) scores at 12 weeks. Results: CBT group showed significantly greater improvement in BDI scores (mean difference: -8.5 points, 95% CI: -10.2 to -6.8, p<0.001). Effect size (Cohen's d) was 0.72. Conclusion: CBT demonstrates significant efficacy for treating depression.

title: Exercise Interventions for Anxiety Disorders: A Meta-Analysis
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of exercise interventions for anxiety disorders. Methods: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. We searched PubMed, PsycINFO, and Cochrane databases through December 2021. Results: 25 RCTs with 1,847 participants were included. Exercise interventions showed moderate effectiveness (pooled SMD: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.35-0.61). Heterogeneity was low (I² = 23%). Conclusion: Exercise is an effective intervention for reducing anxiety symptoms.

title: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction for Chronic Pain: Cohort Study
abstract: Background: Chronic pain affects millions worldwide. Mindfulness-based interventions may provide relief. Methods: Prospective cohort study of 250 patients with chronic pain enrolled in an 8-week MBSR program. Pain intensity measured on Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at baseline and 8 weeks. Results: Significant reduction in pain intensity observed (mean change: -2.3 points on 10-point VAS, p<0.01). 65% of participants reported clinically meaningful improvement. Conclusion: MBSR shows promise for chronic pain management.

title: Pharmacological Treatment of ADHD in Children: Systematic Review
abstract: Introduction: ADHD is commonly treated with stimulant medications, but questions remain about efficacy and safety. Objective: Systematic review of stimulant medication effectiveness in pediatric ADHD. Methods: Searched multiple databases for RCTs comparing stimulants to placebo in children aged 6-17. Results: 42 studies (N=5,234) included. Stimulants showed large effect on ADHD symptoms (SMD: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.75-0.97). Side effects were generally mild. Conclusion: Stimulant medications are effective for pediatric ADHD.

title: Sleep Interventions for Insomnia: Network Meta-Analysis
abstract: Purpose: To compare effectiveness of different sleep interventions for chronic insomnia. Methods: Network meta-analysis of RCTs comparing CBT-I, medication, exercise, and control conditions. Primary outcome: Insomnia Severity Index. Results: CBT-I was most effective (SUCRA: 0.92), followed by medication (SUCRA: 0.71) and exercise (SUCRA: 0.58). CBT-I showed effect size of 0.69 vs control. Conclusion: CBT-I is the most effective intervention for chronic insomnia.

title: Acupuncture for Migraine Prevention: Pilot RCT
abstract: Background: Acupuncture is used for migraine prevention but evidence is limited. Methods: Pilot randomized controlled trial with 60 participants. Intervention group received 12 weekly acupuncture sessions; control received usual care. Primary outcome: migraine frequency. Results: Acupuncture group had 2.1 fewer migraines per month (95% CI: 0.8-3.4, p=0.002). No serious adverse events. Conclusion: Pilot results suggest acupuncture may reduce migraine frequency. Larger trials needed.

title: Diet and Cardiovascular Disease: Prospective Cohort Study
abstract: Introduction: Diet plays a crucial role in cardiovascular health. Methods: Prospective cohort study following 15,000 adults for 10 years. Dietary patterns assessed via food frequency questionnaire. Primary outcome: incident cardiovascular events. Results: Mediterranean diet adherence associated with 30% lower CVD risk (HR: 0.70, 95% CI: 0.62-0.79). Benefit remained after adjusting for confounders. Conclusion: Mediterranean diet associated with reduced cardiovascular disease risk.

title: Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy for PTSD: Case Series
abstract: Background: Virtual reality (VR) offers new possibilities for exposure therapy. Methods: Case series of 12 veterans with PTSD receiving VR exposure therapy. Sessions conducted weekly for 10 weeks. Outcome: PTSD Checklist scores. Results: 10 of 12 participants showed clinically significant improvement (>10 point reduction). Mean reduction: 18.5 points (SD: 8.2). Well tolerated with no dropouts. Conclusion: VR exposure therapy shows promise for PTSD treatment.

title: Smartphone Apps for Mental Health: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Objective: Evaluate effectiveness of smartphone mental health apps. Methods: Systematic review of RCTs testing apps for depression, anxiety, or stress. Results: 28 RCTs (N=4,183) included. Apps showed small-to-moderate effects on mental health outcomes (SMD: 0.38, 95% CI: 0.24-0.52). Effects were larger for apps based on established therapies (e.g., CBT). High heterogeneity (I² = 67%). Conclusion: Mental health apps show promise but quality varies widely.

title: Ketamine for Treatment-Resistant Depression: Expert Opinion
abstract: Introduction: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) affects 30% of depressed patients. Ketamine has emerged as a novel treatment. Discussion: Based on clinical experience and literature review, we discuss ketamine's rapid antidepressant effects. Evidence suggests single infusions can produce rapid symptom relief, though duration is limited. Safety profile is acceptable under medical supervision. Challenges include optimal dosing, frequency, and long-term safety. Conclusion: Ketamine represents important advance for TRD but questions remain.
